ateret-zekenim/1:_: The the Gemara first and later a candle of Shabbat (E. HaTaem 17) but the Tos wrote that the Kabbalah does not depend on lighting them and it can be lit for the first Shabbat and after Hanukkah 27 that they did not accept Shabbat and it looks like a duff per the Tos one should light Hanukkah first only as he wrote that it can be lit later and so the world used to do so (Kmash B.S.A.) who lit a Shabbat candle in his home, it is permissible to light a Hanukkah candle because the Tos should rely on them in times of need, since per their view the acceptance of Shabbat does not depend on lighting it, it is better to light a Shabbat candle first because it is frequent, etc., and also because of a dener of a Shabbat mitzvah for academics and of a Hanukkah mitzvah after the end of sunset, which is permissible to light if he forgets to light the Hanukkah candles until he lights them in his home Shabbat candle as above:
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: (1) On erev Shabbat etc. Some are accustomed to light before Mincha (Rama siman 471 seif 7), and the Levush omitted this because he wrote in Darkei Moshe that our custom is to light between Mincha and Maariv. Nevertheless it appears specifically while the day is still great; but when he sees that if he prays Mincha the time will pass and there will be some prohibition to light, he should light before Mincha, whether in synagogue or at home. The same applies to one who can pray with a minyan in synagogue: he should light at home before Mincha and then go to synagogue. This is specifically after plag haMincha:
eshel-avraham/1:_: Shabbat candle. Whether one may light with Chanukah for the Shabbat candle — see section 9 of Beit Yehudah siman 51:
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (1) [seif 1] On erev Shabbat one lights the Chanukah candle first etc. So too Beit HaGadol: if one lights Shabbat first it is forbidden for him to light Chanukah, for he has accepted Shabbat; and the Tosafot wrote that acceptance is not dependent on lighting and one may light Shabbat first and then Chanukah, for thus they did not accept Shabbat. And Beit Yosef and Tur. Beit Yosef wrote: for practical application it appears to me that one lights Chanukah first, for even according to those who disagree with Beit HaGadol, if he wishes to light Chanukah first he is permitted — end of his words; therefore he ruled thus in the Shulchan Aruch. So too in Darkei Moshe that we practice lighting Chanukah first, and so in our customs — end of his words; and so Bach that the world practiced like Beit HaGadol. So too Birkei Yosef letter 1 that the essential ruling is as Maran ruled, that thereby one satisfies all views; and the Radbaz agreed in responsum siman 457 and elaborated on this. There is also a reason as the essential truth: Chanukah first and then Shabbat candle, for we ascend in holiness, and so it is fitting to practice — end of his words; and so in Bigdei Yeshua that one should not deviate from the Shulchan Aruch's ruling. So too Chayei Adam general rule 154 letter 35. And so above siman 478 end of letter 2 in the name of the Kavvanot; the reason is a secret — see there:
levushei-serad/1:_: Taz s.k. 1 — a man who lights etc. He follows the reason he wrote in siman 263 s.k. 1 that there is no distinction between a woman who lights and a man who lights; and Magen Avraham wrote here that for a woman who lights etc. he follows his reason that he wrote there in s.k. 18 that for a man who lights there is no custom — see there:
shaarei-teshuvah/1:_: In the Shulchan Aruch one lights etc. See in Shevut Yaakov siman 15 at the end that it is forbidden to leave a non-Jew on Shabbat to extinguish the Chanukah candles at night and relight them, for it is not proper to do so since it is complete melacha d'oraisa; and if for pirsumei nisa it is a mitzvah that comes through a transgression. Also we did not find anywhere this mitzvah requires them to burn evening and morning for publicity of the miracle — see there. And see in Birkei Yosef who wrote in the name of Maharash Abuhav responsum kuntres tav yod: one should be careful to pray Mincha on erev Shabbat of Chanukah and then light Chanukah, for Mincha prayer corresponds to the tamid of bein ha'arbayim and Chanukah is a remembrance of the miracle done in the candles of the menorah lit after the tamid of bein ha'arbayim — end of his words:
